chapter: Charley Johnson and the Army band
title: Length of service and war's end
summary: He served about fourteen months from early 1918 to 1919 and first heard 'fini la guerre' in the Meuse-Argonne.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Right. And, how long were you in the Army?
About a year and two months, I guess.
So, you went into the Army in 1917, I gather.
No, the beginning, the first part of 1918.
Then we were mustered out in 1919, and we come back.
So, in other words, the war was over by the time you got out.

Oh, when the war was -- we was in the Meuse Argonne offensive. And at the time, the Meuse Argonne section, and that's the first time I heard the words, 'fini la guerre, la guerre est fini'. Well, we didn't hardly know what it meant, at the time, see?
I see. So, anyway, when you got out, the war was over, it was over in November of 1918, right?
Right. And when you came back to -- where?
